method: Both reviewers read every German string of the current file (u09.json written 28 Sep 01:28, after r2 at 00:43). That covers the title and title.canDo, the Folge (now 11 lines: l10/l11 are new since r2), the gist item and the gloss, and the three inputs (LS1 dialogue and menu, LS2 dialogue, LS3 dialogue and e-mail). It also covers the 6 H1 texts and the strategy card, both speaking parts (instructionsDe, situationDe, cards, openingLine, hintWords, 16 model turns, aiRole), and the S1 situation, taskDe, 5 fields, checklist and modelText. We read the 2 check lines, the 8 redemittel, both aussprache blocks, the story beat and cliffhanger, every endLine, promptDe, option and explanation.de, and the fact record. Outside the unit we read rc.moegen, rc.akkusativ and the 36 lexicon entries allocated to a1.1-u09, with their examples. We solved all 93 authored items blind from promptDe plus options, tiles or audio line: 1 Folge gist, 15 input, 12 structured-input, 33 pool, 16 reserve, 6 H1, 8 check and 2 proof. We also solved the 4 perception items and the 5 S1 fields. We checked the generator slots against the lexicon roles: every lex.glossTyped source is productive, every lex.articlePlural source has a plural, and no dictation source carries `say`. We permuted the tiles of every sentence_building item, V1 questions included, and tried every correction the named category admits. We ran about 200 candidate answers through the real grader. Form fields went through src/components/course-v2/grade.js gradeAnswer exactly as WritingTaskView FormTask builds them, and items went through src/lib/course-v2/checkItem.js. The candidates covered the r2 stop-gap forms and 60 time, day, name and head-count spellings, and every order of ls1-p09. We also ran a paradigm sweep, typing every other present-tense person form of mögen, nehmen and möchte into every typed item keyed on one of them. We compiled a1.1 in memory with scripts/course-v2/lib/compiler.mjs compileLevel. We ran the live normalizeSpeakingTask and buildCoursePartnerPrompt({ level, task }) of netlify/functions/_shared/speakingAI.mjs on the compiled a11-u09-s entry, and read the profile selection in rubrics/speakingV2.mjs. We checked the exam blocks against content/course-v2/registries/lanes/sd1.json: h1 is 6 × abc, 3 options, 2 plays, 32–53 words, text variant; sp2 is cards-ask with 2 topics; sp3 is cards-request with 2 cards; s1 has 5 fields and a 36–48-word situation. We checked every H1 option against its text. We recomputed every sum against the LS1 menu: LS2 20,90, t2 6,40 → 8,90, t6 11,10, check 9,20, S1 head count Olena + 5 = 6. We ran the validator's own knownForms + licensedForms at a1.1-u09 over every German string of the file. We ran a production-surface scan against lexicon roles: redemittel with forTemplate, hintWords, learner model turns, learner cards, micro-output prompts and the modelText. We looked up the allocation of each unknown token in all eight lexicons. We read cast and story against casts/a1.json and against u08 (cliffhanger), u10 (Sophie's call, „Bis Freitag im Restaurant!“, Dresden the day after the birthday) and u11 (the Kochi report). We re-read both sources of fact a1.1-u09-f01 at gesetze-im-internet.de in this session: § 13 PAngV („Bedienungsgeld und alle sonstigen Zuschläge einschließen“) and § 107 Abs. 3 GewO (the Trinkgeld definition). We verified every r2 finding against the current file and the file dates of the engine, checker, lexicon, rule-card and rail files. We compared the trail classes of a1.1-u04 r1–r5 and of the r3 reviews of u03, u05, u06, u07 and u08. We ran no git command and edited no file except this review.

findings.problem: r2 missed this: we tested orders and time forms, not person forms. a1.1-u03 r3-F01 found the class after our r2, measured it at 45 typed items in nine A1.1 units („u09 4“), and u08 r3-F03 confirmed it. Our paradigm sweep finds seven items in u09. check.js calls a one-letter difference a typo unless the last letter differs. The person endings -st and -t differ inside the word (magst/magt, mögt/mögst, nimmst/nimmt), so each of these errors comes back TYPO. ItemView gives one retry, then resolves the same answer as correct and logs it as correct, with no error tag. Three of the seven items drill the person forms of the unit's one new point, g.moegen, and their own explanations teach exactly the endings the grader forgives. The other four drill the vowel-change verb nehmen, including c02 in the scored Check. A grader that accepts the error an item exists to remove is a gate hole that lets a finding class through (§9.4, MAJOR). The unit cannot close it: there is no item field for known wrong forms, and CLAUDE.md forbids patching the checker's job in the data. Stop-the-line is in force for this class.
